purpose: keep the service available through the failure of a component, zone or dependency, by design
entry_criteria: Failure domains (zones, regions, accounts) are known
procedure: Identify single points of failure across compute, data, network and dependencies.
Remove them with redundancy across failure domains, health checks and automatic failover where the objective needs it.
Design state handling: replication mode, consistency and the data-loss window on failover.
Test failover by removing a component or zone in a safe environment and measure the user impact and time.
Document degraded modes and what the service does when a dependency is down.
Review the design when dependencies or load change.
acceptance_criteria: No unmitigated single point of failure remains or each is accepted
validation_method: Cloud architect and service owner review.

validation.check: terminate one instance in a non-production zone and watch the service
list components with a single instance or a single zone
validation.expect: each has mitigation or accepted risk

failure_modes.detection: Outage in one shared service takes everything down
failure_modes.response: Add it to the map and mitigate
Change replication mode or accept the window explicitly

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A service runs in three zones behind health-checked load balancing. Removing one zone in a test keeps error rate under one percent and p95 latency stays within the objective.
